To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

unhealthy weight control behaviors (e.g., dieting and purging behaviors) mediated the association between youth overweight status and emotional and/or social avoidance health-related quality of Life in treatment-seeking youth.

Unhealthy weight control behaviors mediated the association between youth body mass index (weight status) and disease-specific health related quality of life in youth who were overweight and obese, such that higher youth body mass index predicted unhealthy weight control behaviors, which were ultimately related to poorer emotional and social health related quality of live.

weight status is an important and significant predictor of disease-specific health-related Quality of life (HRQL) in overweight and obese youth, and the relationship between weight status and emotional, and social HRQL is mediated, or partially explained, by unhealthy weight control behaviors (i.e., purging, fasting, laxatives, and diet pills).
